To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the extent of inhibition of aggregation during refolding of a recombinant human protein, r-hGH, is dependent on both the mode of refolding (dilution additive vs artificial chaperone) as well as the temperature of the process.

the extent of inhibition of aggregation during refolding of recombinant human growth hormone (r-HGH) is higher when the entire process is carried out under artificial chaperone-assisted mode as compared to the dilution mode, and the extent of inhibition is even higher when the refolding is achieved at 4 degreesC.

(i) CTAB is a more potent additive than alpha-CD in dilution and a better capturing agent than alpha-CD, and (ii) the aggregation can be completely eliminated by a well worked out combination of cold temperature and a suitable stripping agent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method for the recovery of biologically active proteins from inclusion bodies.
the elucidation of factors responsive for protein aggregation and the development of strategies that can be used to minimize aggregation during refolding process.
a systematic investigation of factors responsible for aggregation and refoldability of proteins during refolding process, particularly at relatively high concentrations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the extent of inhibition of aggregation during refolding is highly influenced by the temperature program, the additives and the mode of refolding (dilution or artificial chaperone) used.
the extent of aggregation in protein folding could be controlled by a combination of temperature and the type of additive used.
the aggregation of proteins during their refolding is a complex phenomenon and is a function of many variables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the refolding process of r-hGH was improved by a combination of cold temperature and CTAB.
the use of artificial chaperones in combination with cold temperature is a better option for controlling aggregation during refolding of recombinant human growth hormone.
a combination of cold temperature with artificial chaperone technique would be the most effective approach to inhibit aggregation in the process of refolding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aggregation process during refolding is not only a result of the protein-protein interactions but also a result of the interactions between the proteins and the refolding additives.
, in order to achieve maximum activity yields in refolding, the process should be carried out in a way to minimize both the aggregation and the misfolding of the protein.
the use of cold temperature as an additive in refolding of recombinant protein can be a good alternative to the use of artificial chaperones.
